description: We are 9th-grade students with big goals and strong ambitions. We are passionate about learning, creating, and taking on new challenges. Our goal is to turn our ideas into meaningful results and keep growing together as a team.
summary:
ORBITAL — Mission Architect is an interactive educational web experience created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project invites players to lead a space agency and design an Earth-observation satellite for a chosen mission, such as climate monitoring, disaster response, or ocean health. Users select scientific payloads, balance mass, power, cost, and science value, choose an orbit, and prepare a launch plan.

The experience combines a cinematic launch sequence with an interactive mission simulation. After launch, players monitor battery charge, temperature, communications, altitude, velocity, mission time, and mission success. During flight, they face reproducible emergency scenarios including a solar storm, overheating, and loss of communication. Every decision affects resources and the final mission score.
details: ORBITAL features a detailed Three.js satellite builder with solar arrays, antennas, thermal insulation, cameras, sensors, and ten selectable instruments. It also includes realistic Earth visualization, bilingual Russian/English support, LocalStorage persistence, payload safety limits, and a final Mission Report with telemetry, key decisions, and outcomes. The prototype runs entirely in the browser using HTML, CSS, Vanilla JavaScript, SVG, Three.js, and local assets—no backend or paid APIs required.
